title: Local invertibility of a normalized finite signed product morphism
statement: For a finite purity setting P [def-pur-conventions], a k-scheme T, and integers r,t, let f:F_r tensor F_t to F_(r+t) be any ordinary fixed-scalar sheaf morphism [def-pur-finite-tensor-reduction-data]. Assume that on every coherent signed frame, f sends the pure tensor of ordinary representatives of its r,t basis vectors, after scalar realization, to the sum-degree basis vector [lem-pur-finite-tensor-product-frame-ext]. Then f is an isomorphism. This is conditional local invertibility of a given morphism; it asserts neither existence nor uniqueness of product morphisms.

source.place: Step 2: compatibility with the invertible twist by associativity; expanded local coherent-frame construction of signed products. Stacks sites-modules.tex, section-tensor-product and section-invertible.

proof.text: Trivialize the first line on a pro-etale cover and take coherent ordered powers and dual bases. The realization unit and counit supply ordinary representatives of these bases. The intrinsic tensor comparison takes their pure tensor to a basis of the intrinsic source tensor line.

The assumed normalization says that the realized map sends a local basis to a local basis, so in these charts it is the identity on the coefficient unit. Its local inverse is linear. On overlaps the inverses coincide since each is the inverse of the same restricted morphism. Glue them by the sheaf axiom to get a two-sided inverse.
The realization equivalence reflects isomorphisms, giving IsIso f. Unit and evaluation bases cover zero and mixed signs; the same argument includes the zero ring and empty objects.

mathlib_searches.query: A sheaf morphism of invertible modules sending local basis generators to basis generators is an isomorphism and is uniquely determined
mathlib_searches.results: Eight results, including Sheaf.isLocallyBijective_iff_isIso, GrothendieckTopology.W_sheafToPreheaf_map_iff_isIso and PresheafOfModules.homEquivOfIsLocallyBijective. They provide general sheaf tools, but none supplies coherent signed frame products for these finite fixed-scalar lines.

mathlib_searches.query: Tensor product of signed integer powers of an invertible sheaf with local basis normalization
mathlib_searches.results: Eight results, including CommRing.Pic.mk_tensor and CommRing.Pic.mul_eq_tensor, concern classes of modules or unrelated scheme sections; none is a normalized sheaf product map or its frame detection criterion. Loogle query "tensorPow", "add" had zero hits.

Mathlib search returned numerical zpow identities, no sheaf product. Read NormalizedSignedTensorPowers (categorical products but no coherent-frame normalization), SignedLineOrdinaryConstraints (successive positive powers and evaluation), and FinitePositiveChartFrameExt (positive single-line detection requiring a first chart; imports the item). Blueprint searches "signed tensor" returned four unrelated operation definitions; "coherent frame" returned no node. No duplicate of the three local sheaf steps.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteTensorSheafProductMap_isIso (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u})
    (T : Scheme.{u}) [T.Over (Spec (.of P.field.k))] (r t : ℤ)
    (f : P.finiteTensorFixedSheaf T r ⊗ P.finiteTensorFixedSheaf T t ⟶
      P.finiteTensorFixedSheaf T (r + t))
    (hf : ∀ (V : T.ProEt) (e : P.FiniteTensorFrame T V)
      (x : (P.finiteTensorFixedSheaf T r).obj.obj (Opposite.op V))
      (y : (P.finiteTensorFixedSheaf T t).obj.obj (Opposite.op V)),
      P.finiteTensorSection T r V x = e.basis r 0 →
      P.finiteTensorSection T t V y = e.basis t 0 →
      P.finiteTensorSection T (r + t) V
        (f.hom.app (Opposite.op V) (P.finiteTensorSectionTmul T r t V x y)) =
          e.basis (r + t) 0) :
    IsIso f
